questions.q: Why does pinning a shared module's version matter, according to this lesson?
options: Pinning a module version has no practical effect and is purely cosmetic
Without a pin, an unreviewed change by the module's author — like a renamed variable or dropped resource — lands silently in every caller
Terraform refuses to run terraform init at all if a module is unversioned
Modules are deleted automatically if they aren't versioned within 30 days
questions.explain: It's the same risk Lesson 1 described for an unpinned provider version, one layer up: changes land automatically on the next init -upgrade unless a version is pinned.

questions.q: In `module "network" { source = "app.terraform.io/ltv-academy/network/azurerm" version = "~> 1.2" }`, what does the `version` argument require about `source`?
options: That source be a local file path on disk
That the module have no outputs defined
Nothing — version works identically regardless of how source is formatted
That source be a registry address — the version argument only works for registry-sourced modules
questions.explain: The version argument is only meaningful when a module comes from a registry (public or private); it has no effect on a git or local-path source.

questions.q: How do you pin a git-sourced module to a specific release, since `version` doesn't apply to it?
options: Set a GIT_MODULE_VERSION environment variable before running terraform init
It cannot be pinned — git-sourced modules always resolve to the latest commit
Append a ?ref= query parameter with a tag, branch, or commit SHA to the source URL
Add a separate pin.tf file inside the module folder
questions.explain: A git source is pinned with ?ref=v1.2.0 appended directly to the source URL, not with the version argument.

questions.q: What is Terraform's private module registry?
options: An org-scoped catalog in Terraform Cloud/Enterprise where internal modules are published, visible only within that organization
A public website anyone can browse without an account
A local folder on each developer's machine that syncs automatically
A feature of the open-source Terraform CLI with no relation to Terraform Cloud
questions.explain: The private module registry is part of Terraform Cloud/Enterprise; it works like the public registry but is scoped to one organization's internal modules.

questions.q: How does an internal module get published to a private module registry?
options: By emailing the module's .tf files to HashiCorp support
Private registries publish modules automatically with no versioning step at all
By manually uploading a .zip file through a web form every time it changes
By pushing a semantic-version git tag (such as v1.2.0) to the module's repository
questions.explain: Publishing works the same way as the public registry: pushing a semantic-version git tag makes that version available to call from source.
